What this report is for

Every payer report is the CDPHP report with visuals switched off — that is the model, so a measure missing from CDPHP is missing here too. The page structure mirrors CDPHP so the two can be read side by side. Clinical Outcomes is the one page with visuals; this one and the other three are still empty.

⚠ Blocked on two decisions: what MVP actually asked for, and which CDPHP visuals are switched on for them. Until both are answered there is nothing honest to draw here.

Average and median PHQ-9 across the treatment period

148 members with a Day 0 score. Scores rise after Day 30 rather than falling. On 148 members that is as likely to be noise as a finding, and it is the first thing to check before this page goes anywhere.

All payers, unfiltered, so this tile is the one place on the page that is not cut to MVP. Other payers are labelled rather than named — their outcomes are not ours to disclose in a report that goes to a competitor.

Submission fileThe member-level file the payer actually receives.

mvp_MMddyyyy_PHQ9

Five rows of the shape of the file, not of the file. Every value here is a deliberate placeholder — the names are Kowalski and Nowak, the ids count up from one, the dates of birth are round numbers, and the code column is zeros because 00000 is not a CPT code and 00000-0 is not a LOINC code. The real file is protected health information. Nothing here can be mistaken for a real member, which is the point.
